title: The web app has no CI job, so its tests never run
description:
**Found 2026-09-16 while reviewing a delegated web change.**

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` defines exactly two jobs: `python` and `infra`. The string `web` appears in it **zero times**.

So the web app has **no CI gate at all** — not tests, not lint, not typecheck. `web/package.json` defines all three scripts and nothing runs them.

## Why this matters now

- `web/lib/*.test.ts` currently holds **64 passing tests** that no pipeline executes. They protect the turn-grant payload builder, which is the code path deciding what authority a bot receives.
- [PR #353](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Chatticus/pull/353) is a web-only change to exactly that code. **CI will pass it without running a single web test.**
- Two web changes merged in the last week (#351 assistant-ui spike, #346 the real workspace) were likewise ungated.

A test suite nobody runs is worse than no suite: it reads as coverage in review and catches nothing.

## What to build

A third job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, modelled on the existing `infra` job (lines 55-76) — same `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-node@v4` with `node-version: "22"`, `cache: npm`, `cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json`, and `npm ci` at the root, since this is an npm workspace.

Then, with `working-directory: web`:

1. `npm test`
2. `npm run lint`
3. `npm run typecheck`

## Expect typecheck to be the interesting one

`npm run typecheck` may fail on first run. **If it does, report the errors — do not delete the step, do not add `continue-on-error`, and do not weaken `tsconfig`.** A gate that cannot fail is not a gate. If the errors are real, they become a separate card and this one lands with the two steps that do pass, plus a note.

Do not "fix" type errors by casting to `any` or adding `@ts-ignore`.

## Constraints

- Do not change `web/package.json` scripts.
- Do not touch the `python` or `infra` jobs.
- Do not change any application code. This card is CI configuration only.
- Keep the job independent of the others so a web failure does not mask a python failure.

## Verification

Push the branch and read the actual run. **Do not report success from reading YAML** — this project has repeatedly found things that were green at one layer and broken at a seam. The evidence is a run URL and its job results.

## Done when

A `web` job appears in CI, runs on the same triggers as the others, executes the suite, and demonstrably fails when a web test fails. Prove that last part deliberately if it is cheap to do so.
